title: Kosmitor configuration
description: Every setting an operator can change. kosmitor.config.json holds them all at their defaults; put your changes in kosmitor.config.local.json (or the file named by KOSMITOR_CONFIG), which only needs the entries you change. Secrets never go here: they stay in environment variables.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, for editor hints.

brand.description: The product's name, look and sign-in page. Change these to rebrand the app.

productName.description: Product name shown beside the logo, in page titles, emails, PDFs and exports.

tagline.description: Short line under the product name in the sidebar when no company is open.

logoUrl.description: Image used as the logo (a path under apps/web/public, such as /logo.svg, or a full URL). null draws the built-in shield in the primary colour.

icons.description: Browser tab and home-screen icons. Replace the files in apps/web/public or point these at your own.

ico.description: Fallback tab icon for browsers and tools that ask for /favicon.ico.

appleTouch.description: 180×180 PNG used when the app is added to an iPhone or iPad home screen.

colors.description: Colours. Each palette runs from 50 (lightest) to 900 (darkest); 600 is the main shade.

primary.description: Main brand colour: buttons, links, focus rings, the active page in the sidebar.

accent.description: Secondary accent: success badges, positive figures and highlights.

charts.description: Series colours for charts, used in order.

status.description: Colours of the compliance score gauge.

track.description: The unfilled part of the gauge.

avatarChoices.description: Avatar colours a person can pick in Preferences; a new account is given one at random.

label.description: Its name, read out by screen readers.

initialsFallback.description: Colours for initials avatars of people who have not picked one, chosen by name.

certificateFrame.description: Frame around stock certificates, award certificates and SAFE/note certificates; the faint title behind the text is a pale tint of it.

signIn.description: Words on the sign-in and sign-up pages.

headline.description: Large headline on the right-hand panel.

features.description: The list under the paragraph: a bold lead and the rest of the line.

url.description: Public address of the web app, used for every link in an email. Set it to your real address in production. Environment variable APP_URL wins over it.

port.description: Port the API listens on. Environment variable PORT wins over it.

allowedOrigins.description: Origins the API accepts browser requests from, besides app.url. Environment variable ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma separated) wins over it.

trustProxy.description: Take the client address from the last X-Forwarded-For entry, the one the proxy in front of the server appends. Turn it on only behind exactly one reverse proxy or load balancer (the Azure deployment is); without one, anyone could forge the address recorded in the audit log and on signatures. Environment variable TRUST_PROXY wins over it.

database.description: PostgreSQL. The connection string itself is a secret and stays in the DATABASE_URL environment variable.

poolMax.description: Connections each server process keeps open. Environment variable PG_POOL_MAX wins over it.

mail.description: Outgoing email. The transport (SMTP_URL or ACS_CONNECTION_STRING) is a secret and stays in the environment.

from.description: Sender of every email, as "Name <address>". Environment variable MAIL_FROM wins over it.

signature.description: Name signed at the end of system emails. null uses brand.productName.

smtpTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one SMTP delivery may take.

acsTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one Azure Communication Services delivery may take.

welcomeEmail.description: Email a welcome, once, to each person who creates an account themselves: by signing up, or by a first Google sign-in. Invited people get their invitation instead, and the demo account gets nothing.

welcomeEmailsPerHour.description: Welcome emails the server sends per hour, from every sign-up together, so the sign-up form cannot be used to send email in bulk. Sign-ups over the limit go through without one. Keep it well below the mail provider's hourly limit, so password resets and invitations still go out: a new Azure Communication Services custom domain allows 100 emails an hour. 0 turns them off.

adminResetLinkHours.description: Lifetime of a reset link an administrator creates for a member.

resetEmailsPerHour.description: "Forgot password" emails one address can receive per hour.

inviteLinkDays.description: Lifetime of the link in an invitation email, with which someone new chooses their password.

inviteEmailsPerAddressPerDay.description: Invitation emails one address can receive in a day, from every company together, resends included.

passwordSignIn.description: Offer email-and-password sign-in. Turn it off to allow Google sign-in only.

selfSignup.description: Let anyone create an account from the sign-in page. Turn it off so only invited people and existing accounts get in.

verifyEmail.description: Make someone who signs up open a link sent to their address before they can sign in. Needs a mail transport (SMTP_URL or ACS_CONNECTION_STRING); without one the address is taken as given. Environment variable VERIFY_EMAIL wins over it.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID of type "Web application". Empty turns Google sign-in off. Environment variable GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID wins over it.

allowedDomains.description: Only accept Google accounts on these email domains. Empty accepts any. Environment variable GOOGLE_ALLOWED_DOMAINS (comma separated) wins over it.

demo.description: A card on the sign-in page that hands out a demo login. Create the account with `npm run sample`.

enabled.description: Show the card and prefill the form. Keep it off anywhere the demo password is not meant to be public.

password.description: Demo account password. It is shown to every visitor, so never reuse a real one.

valuationDesk.description: An optional service: companies ask for a new 409A, your internal team approves the request by email before it reaches the evaluators, and the company follows the request in the app. Off by default.

enabled.description: Offer the service. Off hides it everywhere and refuses new requests.

name.description: What the team is called, as it reads after "the" (for example "Acme valuation team"). null uses "<productName> valuation team".

email.description: Where an approved request is sent: one address, or a list of up to 10, one per evaluator. Each address gets an email of its own with the same private link, so no evaluator sees another's address. Replies to the recap and the status emails reach the first. A notice counts once against the per-request, per-company and per-person notices limits, however many addresses it goes to, and once per address against noticesPerHour. Removing an address does not take back a link already sent: it works until a new notice for that request replaces it, or until it expires. null saves approved requests without notifying an evaluator; internal approval is still required. Environment variable VALUATION_DESK_EMAIL, comma separated, wins over it.

approvalEmail.description: Private internal inbox that approves each new 409A request before any evaluator receives it. Configure one email address through VALUATION_APPROVAL_EMAIL or your private local configuration before enabling the valuation desk. The shipped empty value is allowed only while the desk is disabled; enabling it without an inbox stops startup. The address is not exposed in the public browser configuration. The environment variable wins over the file; an empty variable leaves the file setting in effect.

linkOpenDays.description: How long the team's status link works while a request is open.

linkClosedDays.description: How long it keeps working after the request closes.

requestsPerCompanyPerDay.description: New requests one company can make per day.

requestsPerPersonPerDay.description: New requests one person can make per day.

noticesPerRequestPerDay.description: Notices one request can send per day at each stage. Internal approval and evaluator notices have separate allowances, so approval reminders cannot consume the allowance for forwarding to evaluators.

noticesPerCompanyPerDay.description: Notices one company can trigger per day at each stage. Internal approval and evaluator notices have separate allowances.

noticesPerPersonPerDay.description: Notices one signed-in person can trigger per day at each stage. Internal approval and evaluator notices have separate allowances.

noticesPerHour.description: Approval and evaluator emails across all companies per hour, sharing one limit. An approval notice counts once; an evaluator notice counts once for each address in valuationDesk.email, so a longer list sends no more mail. Keep it well below the mail provider's hourly limit, so password resets and invitations still go out: a new Azure Communication Services custom domain allows 100 emails an hour. It cannot be fewer than the addresses in valuationDesk.email.

statusEmailsPerRequestPerDay.description: Emails one request can send the person who asked per day, each time its status changes. 0 turns them off.

reportUploadsPerRequestPerDay.description: Reports the team can upload to one request per day from its page. The app reads the values from each one for the company to check. 0 turns uploads off.

sendCooldownSeconds.description: Wait between two sends of the same request, for approval or to evaluators.

resendCooldownMinutes.description: Wait before a request can be sent for approval or to evaluators again with a new link.

intake.description: The questions a company answers when it asks for a 409A. Keep each value: answers already given are stored by it.

value.description: Stored value. Do not change it once answers exist.

label.description: Words used in emails and summaries.

shortLabel.description: Words on the button in the form.

value.description: Stored value. Do not change it once answers exist.

label.description: Words used in emails and summaries.

shortLabel.description: Words on the button in the form.

plans.description: What the company plans to do soon. Keep a value of NEITHER: it is the answer that needs no timing.

value.description: Stored value. Do not change it once answers exist.

label.description: Words used in emails and summaries.

shortLabel.description: Words on the button in the form.

planTimings.description: When it plans to do it.

value.description: Stored value. Do not change it once answers exist.

label.description: Words used in emails and summaries.

shortLabel.description: Words on the button in the form.

securityTypes.description: The kinds of security a secondary transaction can be in, for the information request's question on buybacks and sales between holders.

value.description: Stored value. Do not change it once answers exist.

label.description: Words used in emails and summaries.

shortLabel.description: Words on the button in the form.

softwareSuggestions.description: One-click answers to "What do you use for your cap table today?".

jsonBodyMb.description: Largest request body the API reads, in MB.

uploadMb.description: Largest document upload, in MB. Files are stored in PostgreSQL.

importMaxRows.description: Rows read from one import sheet.

importMaxSheets.description: Sheets one import takes, across all its files.

importJsonMb.description: Largest import preview or commit request, in MB: it carries every row of every file being imported.

importUnzippedMb.description: Most an .xlsx import may unpack to, in MB, across the parts that are read. A workbook that unpacks to more is refused: a small file that unpacks to gigabytes is a zip bomb.

importMaxTotalRows.description: Rows one import takes across all its sheets and files. Each sheet still reads at most importMaxRows.

ledgerPageSize.description: Transactions and audit entries returned by default.

ledgerMaxPageSize.description: Most transactions and audit entries one request can return; the pages ask for this many.

reportRows.description: Rows a report run returns by default.

reportMaxRows.description: Most rows one report run can return.

reportPreviewRows.description: Rows shown in the report builder preview.

compliance.description: How findings are scored and how early they are raised. Legal limits themselves (the ISO $100K limit, Rule 701, the 83(b) 30 days, the 12-month 409A presumption) are law and not configurable.

scoring.description: The compliance score: it starts here and each finding takes points off.

points.description: Points each finding takes off, by how serious it is.

bands.description: Words for each score range, highest first. The last band must start at 0.

valuationExpiryWarningDays.description: Days before a 409A's twelve months run out that it shows as ending soon.

election83bUrgentDays.description: Days left in an open 83(b) window when it becomes a must-fix finding.

rule701WarnHeadroom.description: Warn when the room left under the Rule 701 limit falls below this share of it (0.2 = 20%).

authorizedSharesWarnRemaining.description: Warn when less than this share of a common class's authorized shares is left (0.05 = 5%).

exerciseWindowWarnDays.description: Days ahead that a closing post-termination exercise window is flagged.

grantExpiryNoticeDays.description: Days ahead that an award's expiration is noted.

noteMaturityWarnDays.description: Days ahead that a convertible note's maturity is flagged.

alerts.description: When overview and SAFE tiles turn to a warning.

optionPoolLow.description: Unallocated option pool below this share of fully diluted (0.02 = 2%).

postMoneySafeOwnershipBanner.description: Post-money SAFEs together promise more than this share of the company: show a banner.

postMoneySafeOwnershipWarning.description: Post-money SAFEs together promise more than this share: the tile turns to a warning.

company.description: What a new company starts with. Each company can change these afterwards.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction of incorporation, also used in documents when a company has none recorded.

legalNameSuffix.description: Added to the company name to suggest its legal name (", Inc.").

commonClass.description: The common share class created with the company.

parValue.description: Par value per share, in dollars.

exerciseRequests.description: Holders can ask to exercise their options from the portal.

portal.description: What the stakeholder portal shows a holder.

vestingSchedules.description: Vesting schedules created with every new company.

name.description: Name shown when picking a schedule.

kind.description: TIME vests over time; FULLY_VESTED vests at grant.

frequency.description: How often shares vest after the cliff.

yearWeights.description: Share vesting in each year, adding up to 1, for back-loaded schedules. null vests evenly.

singleTrigger.description: Share of the unvested balance that vests on a change of control, 0 to 1.

doubleTrigger.description: Share that vests on a change of control followed by a termination, 0 to 1.

equity.description: What new awards, certificates, offers and SAFEs are prefilled with.

optionTermYears.description: Option term for new awards, also assumed for imported options without an expiration. An ISO's default term never goes past the legal 10 years.

postTerminationExerciseMonths.description: Post-termination exercise window for new awards, and the one assumed when an award records none. Under US tax law an ISO exercised more than 3 months after leaving loses ISO treatment, whatever the window; the tax estimates do not model that.

vestingMonths.description: Vesting length for a new schedule.

backLoadedWeights.description: Share vesting each year when "back-loaded" is ticked, adding up to 1.

doubleTriggerWindowDays.description: A termination must fall within this many days of a change of control for double-trigger acceleration.

signerTitle.description: Title of the company signatory on certificates and awards, and on documents the server prepares, when the company has no default signatory.

convertibleSignerTitle.description: Signatory title the "Raise with SAFEs or notes" form starts with when the company has no default signatory.

offerSignerTitle.description: Title of the signer of an offer letter.

offerExpiryDays.description: Days an offer letter stays open.

stockholderConsentThreshold.description: Share of voting shares a stockholder consent needs (0.5 = a majority), above 0. Your charter and the law may require more.

convertibleInstrument.description: Instrument for a new SAFE or note.

noteCompounding.description: Interest compounding for a note that is recorded, or issued without one stated.

raiseNoteCompounding.description: Interest compounding the "Raise with SAFEs or notes" form starts with.

originalIssuePrice.description: Original issue price per share, in dollars.

modeling.description: Starting values of the scenario models.

preMoneyValuation.description: Pre-money valuation of a modeled round, in dollars.

targetPoolPercent.description: Option pool target after the round, in percent.

exitPresetsMillions.description: Exit values offered as one-click presets, in millions of dollars.

exitValue.description: Exit value the waterfall opens with, in dollars.

portalMaxExit.description: Largest exit on a holder's portal chart, in dollars.

portalSalePriceMultiple.description: In the portal's exercise model, the assumed sale price as a multiple of the current fair market value.

tax.description: Rates assumed by exercise and sale tax estimates. They are planning figures, not advice; a holder can change them on the page.

socialSecurity.description: Social Security (0 assumes the wage base is already reached).

defaultAssumptions.description: Assumptions used until a company sets its own.

expectedTermYears.description: Expected term in years. null uses the simplified method for each tranche.

attribution.description: How expense is spread over vesting.

forfeiturePolicy.description: Account for forfeitures as they occur, or estimate them.

locale.description: How the pages, documents, exports and emails write numbers, money and dates. The engine follows US law, so legal amounts stay in US dollars, and compliance findings and the assistant's figures are written US style.
Language tag for number and date formatting, such as en-US or en-GB.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code money is shown in.

importDateOrder.description: How imports read a date like 03/04/2025: auto (month first when unclear), MDY or DMY.

legal.description: Legal wording. Have your counsel check it.

stockLegends.description: Restrictive legends printed on the back of every stock certificate, in order, each when its condition holds: always; restricted (vesting, early exercise or a repurchase right); plan (shares from the equity plan, such as an exercise); notPlan (any other shares); nonUs (a holder with a W-8 on file, a non-US tax country, or a Regulation S issue). A share class's own legend and the company's certificate terms are added after them. Have counsel review them.

convertibleLegend.description: Legend printed before the terms of every SAFE and convertible note.

ai.description: The assistant: people bring their own API key, and each question sends a summary of the cap table to the provider they chose.

enabled.description: Offer the assistant. Turn it off if cap table data must not leave your servers.

models.description: Suggested models; people can type any other.

endpoint.description: Messages API URL, for a gateway or proxy.

models.description: Suggested models; people can type any other.

endpoint.description: Chat Completions API URL, for a gateway or proxy.

models.description: Suggested models; people can type any other.

endpoint.description: Generative Language API base URL; /models/<model>:generateContent is added.

maxOutputTokens.description: Longest answer requested from the model.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one answer may take.

historyTurns.description: Earlier messages sent with each question.

snapshot.description: How much of the cap table goes with each question. Fewer means less data shared and a cheaper call.

examplePrompts.description: Questions offered in an empty conversation.

backup.description: Nightly backups to Azure Blob Storage (apps/server/src/backup-upload.ts). The Azure deployment sets these from Terraform.

container.description: Blob container. Environment variable BACKUP_CONTAINER wins over it.

prefix.description: Start of each dump's name. Environment variable BACKUP_PREFIX wins over it.

drillDatabase.description: Scratch database the weekly restore drill restores into. Environment variable DRILL_DATABASE wins over it.

maxRowDrift.description: Rows per table the restore drill tolerates between the dump and the live database.
